How Salt And Sand Can Lead To Concrete Issues! January 28th, 2021 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: How Salt and Sand Can Lead to Concrete Issues Whether it’s a cracking driveway, pitting concrete sidewalks, or a crumbling stoop, what you put on your concrete during the winter can have a major impact. There are many factors that can play into the concrete around a home falling into disrepair. One primary reason is the soil under the concrete. But, what you put on top of your concrete can make a difference as well. When water freezes and thaws over and over, it can cause the surface of your concrete driveway to crack, pit and crumble. Think of your driveway as a giant sponge. Concrete is porous, so it soaks up water at the surface — maybe from rain or melting snow. When temperatures drop below freezing, water turns into ice, which expands and breaks the walls of those tiny pores, weakening the concrete. You probably won't notice this damage at first. Unfortunately, though, it worsens exponentially with every freeze/thaw cycle until the pitting and flaking become obvious to the naked eye. Sprinkling salt to your driveway and sidewalks doesn't help either. Not only does it assist the freeze/ thaw cycle, but the salt itself accelerates the breakdown of concrete by causing corrosion under the surface, leading to cracked and crumbling concrete. The key to protecting your driveway for the long term is to seal it from the elements. Sealing your driveway may seem like a no-brainer, but many homeowners forget this simple step only to regret it years later when it becomes necessary to replace or resurface their driveway. Foundation issues don’t get better with time, but many people wait an average of five years before they call on a specialist to look at the problem. Here are three reasons why waiting to get your foundation fixed is a bad idea. 1. The problem will get more expensive. Often times, when someone notices a foundation issue, it’s usually something that started small and grew over time. This could be a crack in a poured concrete basement wall, or perhaps you're noticing a gap between the floorboards and the wall. As the problem continues, it will take more effort and resources to bring the foundation back to its most stable condition. Also, the more a foundation falls into disrepair, the more other issues around the home will crop up. These include sticking doors and windows, or even issues with the roof. 2. The issue may become a major safety concern. Next, the safety and stability of a home’s foundation can be compromised the longer a homeowner waits to repair it. Bowing walls are a sign the foundation could cave in – and they often do. Additionally, foundation issues can affect the floors on the levels above the basement, slab, or crawlspace. The flooring could become uneven or bouncy, making it less safe. 3. Your property value may decrease. A new homeowner would assume any responsibility for the home’s foundation. If a foundation issue was flagged during the home inspection, it could indicate a major expense soon. The good news is a repaired foundation is not a red flag for a potential buyer. In fact, there are even instances where a repaired foundation is more stable and stronger than the original construction. In conclusion, homeowners balance a lot of different decisions and priorities when it comes to their homes. This can lead to inaction when they notice a concerning crack in a poured wall, bouncing floors that make it easy to lose balance, or floors separating from the wall. However, fixing a foundation should remain top-of-mind. While the price and inconvenience of a home project might be uncomfortable in the short term, it will restore property value, ensure a safe living space, and – ultimately – result in peace of mind for the homeowner. Mud Jacking November 3rd, 2020 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: If you’re reading this blog, you’ve probably already found some concrete issues around your home and are looking for the right solution to fix these troubles. If the issue is sinking or settling slabs, mud jacking is a technique that’s been around for decades. The process involves mixing a mud and concrete slurry and pumping it under a sinking slab. It’s sometimes called slab jacking or grout pumping. It can also be messy, unpredictable and leave large holes in the concrete where they cut out room for the injection equipment. The materials used can also wash away overtime, causing the same issues all over again. Now, there are modern alternatives to mud jacking, including the technique Davenport Foundation Repair uses – PolyLevel. It’s a foam that in injected under a concrete slab that slowly expands and hardens, leading to a permanent solution that won’t wash away overtime. The ports – or holes where a contractor injects the product under the concrete – are smaller than the size of a dime, much smaller than typical for mud jacking. about_us_our_blog_38164_did_you_know_sag.title: Did you know sagging floors can be a sign of issues in your crawlspace? Here's how we can help. | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair
about_us_our_blog_38164_did_you_know_sag.meta:
A gap between the floor and the baseboard, uneven tilting floors, or a bounce as someone walks across the room - these are signs of sagging or sloping floors in a home.
Unfortunately, sagging or sloping floors are an issue that most often gets worse overtime. It can be a sign of foundation issues within a crawlspace.
Serious damage to your foundation can develop immediately following construction, or years later as changes occur within the soils that surround and support your home. Sagging, uneven floors aren't just unsightly - they can pose safety hazards to those living in the home.
When a crawl space is built, block or brick - or even wood - columns are located throughout the crawl space to support the weight of the structure above. Sometimes these columns settle overtime, and as they sink, they provide less stable support to a home and the floors above. Other times, the columns may have been placed too far apart to begin with, and the support beam - or girder - linking the columns and helping to hold the structure up starts to sag, causing a ripple effect.
Finally, if the columns and other materials inside the crawlspace are made of wood, exposure to natural elements could cause deterioration overtime.
These problems with a foundation are best fixed by a contractor who specializes in crawlspaces. Davenport Foundation Repair has years of experience helping homeowners restore the safety of their homes. We offer exclusive products that can replace the affected columns and beams causing the issue, permanently stabilizing the home's foundation. Our confidence in our work is backed by our lifetime warranty.
The process starts with a no-obligation inspection of the house and a presentation of our findings. To ease worry and redeem peace of mind, schedule your appointment today.

How might unsightly concrete problems affect the curb appeal of a home you're trying to sell September 14th, 2020 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: There’s no doubt 2020 has been a strange year for careers, families and communities – this includes real estate. Across the country, inventory was at historic lows over the spring and summer months as COVID-19 left many people uncertain about their future. But, for those looking to sell, doing so during a period of low inventory could be a good thing. Real estate prices are classic supply and demand economics. Even if people aren’t willing to spend as much on a house, lower demand means they have far less choices in homes. Regardless of what’s happening in the real estate market, homes with curb appeal tend to sell for more money than those that have none. Curb appeal is one of many factors homeowners consider when buying a home – but for some, it’s the most important. In addition to nice, clean siding, and tidy landscaping, the concrete around your house affects the overall curb appeal. Cracked concrete can look concerning to the home’s potential new buyers. Concrete that’s sunken or uneven is a safety concern. If you’re thinking of putting your home on the marketing but are concerned about curb appeal, the good news is most of the time, the concrete can be repaired and restored without the downtime of re-pouring new concrete. Choosing the right contractor can help keep your costs low, while ensuring your project is completed on time. Also, asking the contracting company about available financing options can help keep projects affordable in times of uncertainty. Whether you’re looking to get your home on the market this fall or plan to stay in it for several more years, repairing the concrete around your home will only help with its curb appeal. What goes into the cost of fixing a crack? July 31st, 2020 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: Nearly every home “settles” into place in one way or another after it’s built. This can show up in tiny, hairline cracks along some interior walls. You might even hear your home creaking in the night. These are normal occurrences and not cause for concern. Unless the cracks in the walls continue to grow. That indicates a larger problem, likely with the foundation the home is built on. There is no DIY fix for a foundation problem – it can be a major safety concern and requires a professional. A professional foundation repair contractor will examine the crack and take into consideration any other symptoms of foundation issues, like sticking doors and windows or sloping floors. It might sound like a complicated fix – it is – but how much is fixing that crack going to cost? It’s hard to pin down exactly how much it will cost to fix a crack in your wall. A crack is just one symptom of what could be several different issues with the foundation. Also, the type of foundation you have could also play a role. Basements, crawl spaces, slab on grade, the list goes on. Some types of foundation are more common than others in different parts of the country. But there is one constant that holds true when it comes to foundation fixes: The sooner you address the problem, the less expensive the solution. It takes less manpower and products to fix a foundation that has dropped by an inch on one corner of the house than waiting until it’s sunk 3 inches or more before fixing it. This holds true for virtually all foundation problems. In almost 100 percent of homes, the issues you see only get worse or more noticeable over time. Our company permanently fixes home foundations every day. Our team is professionally trained to diagnose complex problems and implement the right solutions. Don’t get sticker shock before you have a professional come out and give you a quote. The peace of mind, quality of life and safety you are looking for in your home is priceless, but if diagnosed soon enough might not cost as much as you think. Why sidewalks might become uneven and who it impacts. July 31st, 2020 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: You probably don’t spend much time thinking about the sidewalk in front of your home. It’s not so much for you as it is for the pedestrians around your neighborhood. However, the sidewalk on your property is your responsibility to maintain. There are a few factors that could cause a sidewalk to need repairs. Rain can wash away the dirt underneath the concrete sidewalk slabs, causing them to sink or settle. In dryer months, the soil can dry out and shrink. This can cause concrete to crack and potentially become a trip hazard. Regardless of the reason for repairs, the safety of your sidewalk is important. Many people use the pathway, whether it’s to get to work or to exercise. Children might use your sidewalk to get to and from school. In many places, it’s the home owner’s responsibility to repair the concrete sidewalk on their property. Often times, the sooner you get it fixed, the less expensive the cost will be. about_us_our_blog_37305_what_kind_of_wea.text: What kind of weather have you been experiencing in your region | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » What kind of weather have you been experiencing in your region What kind of weather have you been experiencing in your region July 2nd, 2020 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: In the summer months, a lot can happen to the concrete in and around our homes. And with more people out and about, concrete issues might feel more noticeable – and more annoying. From a sunken sidewalk slab to a cracked concrete driveway, the climate of the region has a direct impact on the soil and, ultimately, the concrete on top of it. It’s not uncommon for many regions to experience a lot of moisture in the early summer months. The rain saturates the soil and can soften it, making concrete slabs sink. Rain and water can also wash away the dirt under and around concrete. This erodes the support underneath the concrete, causing it to crack and drop. Dry weather and the hot summer sun can also dry out the soil around your home. As the moisture in the soil evaporates, the dirt shrinks – or takes up less space – impacting the stability underneath the concrete. Much like when dirt is washed away, the lack of support can cause the concrete to crack and fall. While it may only drop a few inches or centimeters, it can dramatically impact the safety and quality of life for those who walk on it. While weather patterns might feel like a never-ending cycle of concrete problems, there are simple and permanent fixes. Our company has helped countless homeowners by lifting their sunken sidewalk slab, repaired their cracked driveway and, ultimately, restored their curb appeal and safety around their home. . Is It Worth the Investment? Waterproofing New Construction. Is It Worth the Investment? July 12th, 2019 Categories: Most of the time homeowners are reaching out to us "after the fact" when they're already seeing the effects of groundwater seeping into their basement. Oftentimes the result can be very expensive, especially if the basement is already finished. But every once in a while we do get that phone call from a homeowner who is just beginning to build their dream home. Sometimes these homeowners have already been told that due to soil conditions and water table levels in the area they may want to consider being proactive on protecting their investment. Sometimes homeowners have been referred to us by others in the neighborhood who have had to call us to address their water issues. In other instances, they may start noticing water issues already rearing their ugly head as the foundation is being put in. Whatever the reason, being proactive and bringing in waterproofing experts early in the building process can protect your investment, and save you from potentially expensive and extensive repairs down the road. Putting in place water safeguards during the building process could cost a homeowner a few thousand dollars, but it can save them thousands more down the road. Waterproofing existing homes can involve removing flooring, sheetrock, and cutting into concrete to install proper drainage systems which can be as much as double the cost of waterproofing during construction. Installing a Below-Floor Drain For a typical basement, our WaterGuard® system is the ideal choice for waterproofing. This French drain is designed to be installed below the floor slab, resting on top of the foundation footing. This keeps this drainage system out of the "mud zone", where drains can clog. Sections of WaterGuard® are placed on the footing, resting on a bed of drainage stone, and the floor is installed above it. A wall flange extends 3/8" above the floor, allowing the drain to collect water leaking from the basement walls and divert it away from the home by way of an exterior discharge line. The photo below shows the WaterGuard system recently installed in a new construction in Kamas, UT . Consult an Expert Your home is one of your biggest financial investments. Whether you are building a new home, looking to purchase an existing one, or want to protect the one you are currently in, it's important to consult a waterproofing company you can trust. The experts at Davenport Foundation Repair have helped thousands of homeowners throughout Utah with their foundation repair and waterproofing needs. We offer free estimates by our highly trained foundation specialists. We also offer financing options. Call our office today to see how we can help you protect your investment. about_us_our_blog_32619_overlooking_this.meta: Sinking driveways and settling foundations are a headache no homeowner wants to deal with. Sometimes adjusting one small detail on your home can make a huge difference in preventing costly damages down the road.
heads: Overlooking This One Small Detail Could Damage Your Home and Driveway
about_us_our_blog_32619_overlooking_this.text: Overlooking This One Small Detail Could Damage Your Home and Driveway | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » Overlooking This One Small Detail Could Damage Your Home and Driveway Overlooking This One Small Detail Could Damage Your Home and Driveway August 14th, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: Most homeowners are already aware of the importance of proper drainage for the water coming off the roof of the house. It’s necessary to have a properly installed system of rain gutters to collect and channel the water from the roof, and downspouts to then funnel that water away from the house. Many times when our foundation specialists go to a home to assess foundation settling and/or sinking driveways we find that improper downspouts are the culprit. Here are some mistakes made when placing downspouts. Too close to the foundation If the downspout is placed close to the foundation it can lead to damage to the foundation such as settling foundations and water in the basement. It’s important to make sure the downspouts channel the water at least 10’ from the foundation to an area that slopes away from the home in order to reduce the chance of compromising the foundation. Placing the downspout on the driveway A common mistake is to place the downspout on the driveway. The water will then seep into the joints of the driveway and eventually cause the concrete to sink. Another issue is the pitting, flaking and cracking of the concrete that results from water pooling up on the driveway and freezing and thawing repeatedly. Placing the downspout on or next to the driveway Placing the downspout next to the driveway can lead to erosion of the soil around and underneath the driveway. As the soil becomes more compromised this will cause voids to form under the driveway which will eventually cause those areas to sink. Not only is this unsightly, it is a tripping hazard as well. If the ground around a home does not slope enough to move the water a proper distance from the home, it may be necessary to extend downspouts underground in order to prevent more costly damage in the future. The water can be moved through pipes to a better location on the property to release the water or carry it to a location in the yard where it can be released using a pop-up drainage emitter. If your home already has underground drainage installed, it’s important to know what type of pipe was used and where the water is being released. If there is no external outlet for the water, it’s possible it is saturating the soil around the foundation. Some companies will use black corrugated pipes underground to channel the water away. The grooves inside these pipes will actually collect and trap debris and become clogged over time. The flexibility of the black pipe also makes it difficult to keep it level underground creating dips in the path of the pipe that will also trap debris and keeps water from flowing freely. Davenport Foundation Repair uses rigid pipe that allows the debris to continue to move through with the water, preventing build-up and clogs. Our highly trained foundation specialists can come to your home to assess the drainage and other foundation and concrete needs and recommend a plan of action to protect your investment, and ultimately your family. Davenport Foundation is Gephardt approved and has an A rating from Angie’s List and BBB. We are built on a foundation of honesty, integrity and responsibility. Trust your home to the local experts. Why You Should Fix It Before You List It Foundation Problems? Why You Should Fix It Before You List It July 31st, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: The reality is that the foundation is truly the base of your home. It is the indicator of how strong, stable and safe the home is. So when homeowners are considering selling a home with foundation problems they have to ask themselves “Should I repair foundation problems before I sell?” It’s a difficult question but one that makes a huge impact on the actual sale of the home. As homes age there will always be some level of settling that occurs, usually due to soil changes that continue over time. You may notice signs of settling within your home, whether it’s cracks in the walls or concrete, leaks in the basement, uneven floors, doors and windows that stick, or even ceilings or window sills that separate from the walls. Bring in professionals to assess your foundation While some of the cracks in your home may be cosmetic issues, they could also be indicators of more serious structural foundation problems. It’s important that you bring in a professional to assess whether the signs of settlement that you are seeing are serious. You can reach out to structural engineers or a local foundation repair company, such as Davenport Foundation Repair, to come to your home and do a full assessment and let you know what your options are for repair. If a homeowner is aware of foundation problems they are legally obligated to disclose this information to potential buyers. Once you know the extent of the issues you can determine whether to repair them before you sell the house, or sell it as-is. Maintaining property value and appealing to potential buyers are things to consider when making that decision. Selling your home at market value The goal of sellers is to get as much for their home as possible. While it would be nice to sell it at market value, foundation problems can be expensive to repair. The signs of settling will be noticed by a buyer’s home inspector and you can expect the buyer’s offer to be lowered to compensate for the repairs they will have to do. Foundation problems can lead to a 10 – 20% reduction in price, if not more. Improving your chances of selling Many potentials homeowners will be scared off by a home with foundation issues. They may not be wanting to take on a home in need of major repairs that they will have to deal with and pay for once they purchase it. And some lenders will not approve a home loan unless the foundation repairs are made. Should you choose to sell the home as-is, you most likely will need to lower your price substantially and find buyers who are looking to flip homes in order to sell your home quickly. Don’t DIY your foundation repairs Properly repairing foundations is not something the average person can do. We receive calls regularly from people who have tried to repair cracks and gaps themselves but find that what they have done is not enough. You need professionals trained to handle foundation problems to come in and do it right the first time. The longer foundation problems are left untreated, the worse they get and the cost to repair them increases. Whether in West Jordan, Woods Cross, Brigham City, or St. George, the Davenport Foundation Repair team handles sinking foundations every day across the state of Utah. about_us_our_blog_32150_what_happens_in_.meta: Moisture in your basement does not stay in the basement. It affects the air you breathe throughout your home, and can leave you breathing in mold.
heads: What Happens in the Basement Doesn't Stay in the Basement
about_us_our_blog_32150_what_happens_in_.text: What Happens in the Basement Doesn't Stay in the Basement | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » What Happens in the Basement Doesn't Stay in the Basement What Happens in the Basement Doesn't Stay in the Basement June 25th, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: What gives the basement that "basement smell" we all know and hate? It's the result of moisture and humidity in the basement. Some of the signs of a wet basement include that musty smell, condensation on the windows or pipes, damp walls or floors, and crystalline deposits on the concrete. Unfortunately it not only smells bad, but it leads to issues throughout the home that can affect your quality of life and even your health. The Stack Effect Warm air rises. As it rises, it leaks out of the upper levels of your home. This process creates a suction that pulls air from the lower levels, such as the basement, to replace the air that has leaked out of the upper levels. Known as the "stack effect," this creates an airflow from the bottom of your house to the top. Up to 50% of the air you breathe on the first floor comes from the basement. So, whether you spend time in your basement or not, your basement air is affecting you and your family, and even your pets. You are breathing in that basement air all of the time. The Mold You Breathe Humidity and moisture in your basement can lead to several issues throughout your home including dust mites, sticking doors and windows, paint peeling, condensation, and more. But one of the scariest impacts is on the health of your family due to mold created by a damp basement that is then moved throughout the house due to the stack effect. And that moisture doesn't just happen in the wet months, it can happen year round. When it's hot and humid in the summer, rain or not, our basement may be the wettest it has been all year. Doctors will tell you there's no such thing as good mold in a home. The Centers for Disease Control (CDC) says mold exposure can cause nasal stuffiness, throat irritation, coughing or wheezing, eye irritation, or in some cases, skin irritation. Some studies have even linked mold exposure to asthma in otherwise healthy children and adults. People who have mold allergies and individuals with compromised immune systems can suffer more serious effects. Break the Mold Mold can be controlled. You need to remove the existing mold and address the source of moisture. If you have noticed any signs of moisture or dampness in your basement, you should call a waterproofing expert. When you call Davenport Foundation Repair , one of our highly trained Foundation Specialists will assess your home to determine the source of moisture in your basement and then consult with you on the solutions available. Together you will choose the option that is best for you and your home. We pride ourselves on being able to restore peace of mind and quality of life for our clients. We offer free estimates , so call us today to schedule one. about_us_our_blog_32005_the_dirt_behind_.text: A look at the reasons foundations settle | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » The Dirt Behind Foundation Settling The Dirt Behind Foundation Settling June 11th, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: It seems more and more homes are seeing some type of damage as the result of foundation settlement. The most shocking cases involve brand new homes that are settling within the first few years of being built. A recent article by Consumer Reports states that 15% of new homes experienced structural problems. So what is the real culprit behind the alarming number of foundation problems? Let's dig deeper to get a better look at the culprit. Let's dig into the soil. Most often, movement occuring within your home can be attributed to changes in the soil beneath and around the foundation. These include changes to the moisture content or the density. Your home is most likely sitting in and on multiple layers of soil, both native soils and man-moved soils. Some of the layers may be silt, some may be sand, and many are made of clay. Each layer has the potential to be impacted by different factors after the home is built. When the various layers and areas settle at different rates, the damaging effects of settlement occur. Here's a look at some of the soil changes that ultimately can lead to settlement: Drying of Soil. Some soil, particularly clay, tends to shrink when it dries. Factors such as lack of rain, periods of drought, or even shrubs and trees planted too close to the foundation can reduce the moisture content of the soil. Excess Moisture. When soils become too wet or saturated they can swell and soften which leaves them unable to support the weight of the structure, or can wash out leaving unsupported voids under the surface of the home. Poorly Compacted Soil. If the existing, native soil under a home is weak or if the fill soil that has been brought in to back-fill around the foundation is poorly compacted, the soils can compress beneath the weight of the foundation. When movement occurs as a result of shrinking, swelling or softened soils beneath the foundation or the soil around the foundation begins to push against the foundation walls, cracks will begin to appear in the foundation, floor slabs, or the drywall in your living space. When you notice these changes you should get the underlying issues addressed as soon as possible. Foundation problems only get worse and more expensive with time. The trained and certified Foundation Specialists at Davenport Foundation Repair can inspect your home and sit down with you to determine the best solution that meets your needs. Our solutions can help restore value to your home, improve your quality of life and most importantly, restore your peace of mind. about_us_our_blog_31558_landscaping_tips.text: Landscaping Tips for a Dry Basement | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » Landscaping Tips for a Dry Basement Landscaping Tips for a Dry Basement April 13th, 2018 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: Living in Utah we know that there’s no controlling Mother Nature. Because we do live in a desert we love the moisture Spring weather brings us. While our yards and water supply need the moisture, there are also potential problems like wet basements. Some of these risks can be reduced with proper landscaping. Here are some tips that can help prevent flooding. Make sure water flows AWAY from your house Water flows downhill, so if your home does not have a proper grade to lead water away from the house it will cause puddles to form around the foundation. If there are areas where water is pooling near the foundation and adjusting the slope of your yard is not an option, you may need to look at installing channels or adding berms to redirect the water in those areas. Install gutters and downspouts properly It’s important to make sure any water coming off the roof drains properly. If your house does not already have rain gutters, install them right away. Downspouts need to extend 4 – 6 feet away from the house to ensure water is directed away from the foundation. Add rocks and gravel. Rocks and gravel can be placed along the foundation to reduce moisture retention. Do not place mulch next to your foundation as this will keep the area around your foundation moist. Rocks and gravel can be a nice landscaping element while reducing your risk of a wet basement. Do not plant bushes and shrubs next to the foundation. Bushes and shrubs can prevent proper evaporation of moisture along the foundation. Place plants that need less water next to the foundation. Don’t plant shrubs within 5 feet of the foundation and make sure all trees are at least 25 feet from the house as well. While these landscaping tips can reduce your risk of water seeping into your basement, they are by no means fail-proof. If you find that you have a wet basement it is important to bring in experts to repair the problem areas as soon as possible in order to prevent more expensive foundation issues down the road. Give us a call to schedule a free estimate from one of our foundation specialists. about_us_our_blog_31234_why_wellduct_may.text: Why WellDuct may Be Your Basement's Best Solution | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » Why WellDuct may Be Your Basement's Best Solution Why WellDuct may Be Your Basement's Best Solution March 8th, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: Spring is on its way! Though the winter has been mild, we expect several spring showers to bring the much needed water to our desert climate. Sometimes that water finds its way into our home’s basements and crawlspaces. Leaky basements are never a good situation, and can affect the value of a home if not properly repaired by trained professionals. Water can come through cracks in the walls, improperly sealed windows or through window wells. When a basement window well does not have sufficient draining, is improperly graded or becomes clogged with debris, water can seep into the basement walls. Creating a drain out of the window well gives homeowners the best chance of avoiding issues caused by leaky window wells. If you're not interested in replacing your basement windows and/or window wells, Davenport Foundation Repair has a solution called WellDuct. Our WellDuct Window Well Drain product establishes a drain from the window well to a drain on the inside the wall like our WaterGaurd system. The process including drilling a hole under the window, in the foundation wall and installing a strainer on the exterior of the foundation. The WellDuct is a vertical piece of ducting that is attached and sealed to the interior foundation wall from a perimeter drainage system to the window well. WellDuct is then connected to the drain system, such as our WaterGaurd system, where water can drain to the sump pump. At Davenport Foundation Repair we have a variety of waterproofing products to make your basement safe and dry. We offer a lifetime written warranty on many products. about_us_our_blog_30813_the_advantages_o.text: The Advantages of our Push Pier System | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » The Advantages of our Push Pier System The Advantages of our Push Pier System January 25th, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: When and why are Push Piers needed to fix a home’s foundation? What do they provide? Will they work? These are just some of the questions we answer every day for our customers. Sometimes the jargon associated with the repairs can be overwhelming, but our Foundation Specialists will answer any questions you may have, show you videos to see how our products work, and offer brochures so you can review the information you received during their visit. The Push Pier System that we use is designed to offer stability, security, and integrity to your home’s foundation. Supportworks, our parent company that designed this system, is a network of the most knowledgeable and experienced foundation repair and new construction contractors in North America. Using their shared knowledge and experience, they have created a system that uses high-strength, round steel tube sections and brackets that are designed to stabilize and lift a sinking or settling foundation. A foundation bracket is used against the existing footing and the pier tubes, or sections, are driven hydraulically through the bracket and into the soil below using the combined structural weight and any contributory soil load as resistance. The pier sections are driven until a suitable load bearing layer is reached. The structure then either begins to lift, or the target pressure is reached. The weight of the structure is then transferred from the unstable soil, which caused the settling, to the foundation brackets, through the piers and to firm load bearing soil or bedrock. There are several advantages to using our Push Pier System. Our system is designed with corrosion protection. The pier tubes are made with a triple-layer, in-line galvanized coating. The pier bracket, external sleeve, and pier cap are also available with a hot-dip zinc coating for galvanized protection. The coil rod and heavy hex nuts are zinc plated. Other advantages of our Push Pier System include the fact that our portable equipment allow for installation in areas where there is limited access to the foundation. Our piers are individually load tested during installation to make sure each pier is stable and secure. Our Piering System comes with a 25 year warranty. We understand your home is your biggest investment. We want to ensure it’s safe, secure, and structurally sound for years to come. Davenport Foundation Repair has been repairing foundations for over 25 years and is a leader in the industry. If you are concerned about your home’s foundation, call us for a free estimate. We’re the local experts. about_us_our_blog_30731_smartjacks_may_b.text: SmartJacks™ May Be the Solution to Your Sinking Floor | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » SmartJacks™ May Be the Solution to Your Sinking Floor SmartJacks™ May Be the Solution to Your Sinking Floor January 15th, 2018 by Denise Hassett Categories: Here's an example of a crawlspace area where SmartJacks would be ideal to use. What is a SmartJack™? A SmartJack™ is an adjustable steel pier designed to repair sinking floors, sinking girders and settling piers. SmartJacks™ are ideal for areas where there isn’t a lot of space or where access is limited, such as a crawlspace. They can usually be installed in one day. Foundation issues are common and are noted by sagging, sloping floors, doors and windows that don’t easily open, and cracked drywall. Davenport Foundation Repair’s SmartJacks™ system is often needed when the floor of a home’s framing is spanned too far apart causing sagging. SmartJacks™ are also helpful when repairing the home where the floor has been compromised by rotted beams, or where footings have been installed improperly and have sunk. In some cases, foundations are impacted by the weight being added to floor systems that aren’t able to handle the heavy load. No matter the cause, we have a cost-effective, permanent solution. Installing SmartJacks™ is something our crews do often. We have recently repaired homes in Logan, UT , Cottonwood Heights, Utah, Woodland, Utah, Park City, UT , Farmington, UT , Salt Lake City, UT and Bloomington, Utah. The installation process is fairly straightforward. Our crew will dig a hole for each SmartJack™ needed and compact a structural stone footing in place. The SmartJack™ is cut to size and installed under the sagging floor. An adjustable screw then jacks up the floor to level. The adjustable screw can be adjusted in the future as needed. Should You Worry If Windows and Doors Won't Close? December 1st, 2017 by Denise Hassett Categories: Picture Above: Exterior Wall Crack Due to Foundation Settling We are often asked about the signs that a structure has foundation issues. Sometimes the signs that there are problems with a structure’s foundation begin subtly. One sign, which could be especially problematic during the cold, winter months, is doors and windows not closing properly. If it takes extra force to open and close a window, the structure may have a foundation issue. Other signs include cracks in the top corners of the doors and windows, door and windows that become out of square, doors with locks that no longer work correctly and uneven or sagging floors. Some of the most common foundation issues that lead to sticking or jamming doors and windows are related to soil settlement in the foundation and crawl space supports that have settled, shifted or deteriorated. Our warrantied foundation piering system is a great solution to foundation issues. Cracks that run along the window and door openings can be signs of foundation settlement. These cracks do not resolve themselves and often become much worse, potentially leading to severe structural damage. When soils settle cement slabs and foundations often crack. Wood framing can bend or twist. Drywall may crack and exterior stone or brick may begin to show cracking as well. By installing piers around the structure to secure it, our piers extend into stable ground and attach to the structure’s foundation with settle brackets. This process allows structures to be jacked back to their original placement. Once raised back, the cracks in the walls, windows, masonry and around the doors will close. If a structure is sinking due to issues with its crawl space, our Smart Jacks are a great solution. Crawl space structures sink due to lack of support, rotting floor joists and weak soil. Warning signs that a crawl space has been compromised include sinking and sagging floors, walls that pull away from the floor and doors and windows that are difficult to open and close. Installing Smart Jacks allow support to be restored. Repairing this issue starts with digging a hole for each support and creating a base of engineered fill. Then a pre-cast concrete base is installed on top of the fill, and the support jack is mounted on top. We rely on windows and doors opening properly to ensure good ventilation and safety. Having repairs done correctly ensures structural safety. If you are seeing signs of settling please call us for a FREE, no-obligation estimate. about_us_our_blog_30358_polylevel_vs_the.meta: Here are some helpful facts to know about the different ways to repair sunken concrete.
about_us_our_blog_30358_polylevel_vs_the.text: PolyLEVEL vs. the Alternatives | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » PolyLEVEL vs. the Alternatives PolyLEVEL vs. the Alternatives November 16th, 2017 by Denise Hassett Categories: YouBlog When it comes to lifting concrete, we have the best product around. Not only do we have smaller injection ports than other companies, meaning smaller, less noticeable holes in your concrete, we also offer a minimally invasive, long lasting, cost-effective solution with our PolyLevel injection foam. We are the only Utah company using the exclusive 3/8 of an inch injection ports. The holes we drill to inject the foam under concrete slabs to lift them are about the diameter of a ballpoint pen. Other companies use 5/8 of an inch injection port, about the diameter of a dime. We often receive phone calls asking if we do mudjacking to repair sunken concrete. Mudjacking is a process where a slab of concrete is lifted by pumping concrete (known in the industry as mud) underneath the slab to be lifted. While this is a solution to lifting concrete, it isn’t long lasting, is often disruptive and does not have the ability to dam up exit points. A second alternative is total replacement of the concrete. This is an expensive alternative and while some concrete slabs are beyond repair, many times PolyLevel foam can be used to provide a fix. This is one of the great benefits we provide with our FREE, no obligation estimates. Our knowledgeable foundation specialists can come to your home and give you the best repair solutions. Our PolyLevel foam can often provide permanent, cost-effective solutions without replacement. There are many benefits to using PolyLevel foam over the alternatives. These include the ability to provide precision lifts, is minimally disruptive and you can use the area 30 minutes after the process is completed. PolyLevel injection foam has the ability to dam up exit points, can be applied in standing water, and it is environmentally friendly. If those aren’t enough reasons to try it, Davenport Foundation Repair offers an extended three year warranty. There are so many reasons why PolyLevel foam is a very cost-effective in comparison to other repair methods. The white port is our old 5/8 inch port. Do you have uneven concrete? We use a unique PolyLevel injection foam to lift driveways, sidewalks, patios, steps, garage floors, pool decks, tennis courts and more. And now, we have a unique, new product that will better serve our customers. We are the ONLY local concrete lifting company with 3/8 inch injection ports. What does this mean for our customers? The port is the small plastic piece used to get the foam into the concrete to lift it. A hole must be drilled into the concrete to insert the ports. The holes we drill are only 3/8 of an inch. Other companies use ports that are up to one inch. This means once the concrete has been lifted, and the drill holes have been filled, the places we drilled into the concrete to lift it are virtually unnoticeable. Our new injection ports create a stronger connection between the port and the injection gun, producing a better seal and eliminating product blow out. The PolyLevel process is minimally invasive, is lightweight, and the area lifted can be used within 30 minutes. In addition to being used in residential settings, PolyLevel foam can also be used on roads, rail roads, airports, parks, schools and hospitals where ADA compliance is necessary. The PolyLevel foam will not wash out or leech into the groundwater. It is environmentally benign and will not reactive with other elements that may be present under the concrete slabs. Besides lifting concrete, the foam also seals leaks, making it a great repair option for some homeowners. Our new 3/8 inch ports are just one more way we are better serving our customers. We provide free estimates to homeowners and offer a three year warranty on our PolyLevel jobs. As the exclusive Utah company offering smaller port sizes, we are able to continue leading the industry with cutting edge technology. What is FlexiSpan? August 24th, 2017 by Denise Hassett Categories: If you notice cracks in your foundation walls, your first reaction may be to panic, especially if there is water seeping through those cracks. Davenport Foundation Repair deals with foundation cracks daily, and has the tools and expertise you need to fix them. Small cracks are common and occur naturally as the concrete cure s. While these cracks usually do not threaten the foundation, some small foundation cracks can let water into your basement or crawlspace. So how do we fix it? One solution is our patented FlexiSpan crack seal. It is a special polyurethane polymer sealant that is put over cracks to prevent further damage, or water coming into the basement. It stays permanently bonded and will never dry out. We warranty it for seven years. It works well with our other products such as our WaterGaurd interior drainage system or our TripleSafe sump pump . Together our products provide total basement or crawlspace waterproofing. While there are other products on the market such as epoxies or urethane injections, they are not able to bend and stretch with foundation movement. We also do not seal cracks from the outside of the home due to the extreme heat and cold weather conditions in Utah. Epoxy on the outside of a foundation is not permanent and will need to be redone several times over the lifetime of the home. As concrete walls expand and shrink slightly through freeze/thaw and wet/dry cycles, the bonds of these materials will fail, leading to re-cracking or new cracks forming farther on down the wall. When this happens water leaking will begin again. Our products provide permanent, cost-effective, and are warrantied. We are your local foundation repair experts. If you are experiencing cracks in your foundation, call us today for a free, no obligation quote, 1-801-569-2302 . We know there are many home repair professionals in our area, and that many people shop around for the professional that best fits their job, needs and budget. What is Efflorescence? July 26th, 2017 by Denise Hassett Categories: Efflorescence occurs when moisture seeps through the concrete foundation floor or wall leaving behind crusty, white, salt deposits. As concrete cures, it shrinks. The curing of concrete basement walls can continue for six months to ten years (in extreme cases) after the home has been built. It’s common for small cracks to occur during the curing period. Those cracks could potentially let water into your home. Even when the surfaces of your basement walls and floors look dry, it’s likely that moisture is entering the basement continually through the concrete in the form of water vapor. Other signs that there is water moisture or vapor in your basement include mold and musty smells in the basement and rust on your pipes, tools, or other metal in the space. Efflorescence can be removed by brushing the concrete with a wire brush or low-pressure washing and then rinsing the surface. However, that won’t stop it from occurring again. The most permanent and cost-effective solution is to have s install a moisture barrier on your walls and floors. A sump pump is also very helpful to redirect water outside of the home. In some cases homeowners will benefit from installing an Energy-Efficient Dehumidifier. You can read more about our moisture barrier products here . Read about our sump pump products here . Read more about our Energy-Efficient Dehumidifier here. Davenport Foundation Repair services the entire state of Utah including Logan, Ogden, Salt Lake, Farmington, Granstville, Tooele, Riverton, Nephi, Delta, Richfield, Cedar City, and St. George. We also offer a 25 year warranty on our full waterproofing system. The warranty is transferable to a new homeowner if you sell your home. We are your local expert. Call us today for a free estimate! People are planning fairy house making parties, searching for hidden fairy houses, and scouring Pinterest for ideas on how to create their own. If you’re tired of hearing “I’m bored!” or “There’s nothing to do” creating your own fairy house (or neighborhood) is a great summer project. This is a great lesson in creativity, engineering, decor, and architecture. Begin by scouting out a great location. Location, in any housing situation, matters! You can house a whole fairy community at the base of a tree, a cluster of rocks or under a rose bush. Next, gather materials from you home and yard such as sticks, pebbles, grass, feathers, buttons, pine cones, fabric and ribbon. Like any good home, the Fairy House should have a strong foundation. Use a flat rock, piece of board or flat sticks. Each person can create their home using simple objects found around the house. Craft stores also sell inexpensive objects to add to your home, or you can even make them from clay, cardboard or fabric. The possibilities for creativity are endless. And it’s a good lesson in learning the importance of a strong foundation while strengthening the foundation of those you are creating with. Read This! Buying or Selling a Home? Read This! May 25th, 2017 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: Let us take the stress out of buying or selling your home. Selling or buying a home can be stressful, especially if the Home Inspection reveals an issue. If your home, or potential home, has a foundation issue, don't despair. Let us provide permanent, cost-effective solutions. We have over 35 years of experience dealing with cracked and settling foundations. You don't have to solve the problem alone! We have a team of expert in-house specialists that are here to help you identify and solve your issues with warrantied products and services. If you own the home, we provide free, no-obligation foundation repair quotes throughout the state of Utah. If you are the potential home buyer, we offer low cost foundation inspections. The results from our inspection can often be used to negotiate a better purchase price. We can fix bowing walls, cracked walls and foundations, water in the basement or crawlspace, uneven floors and foundations, restoring the integrity of your home. Don't despair! You have a local expert on your side. Are You Experiencing.... May 15th, 2017 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: Cracks such as these are a warning that your home needs foundation repair. There are several warning signs that your foundation may need some repair. Cracks in the foundation itself Cracking on the interior or exterior walls A leaning or tilting chimney Uneven or sloping floors Door or windows that are difficult to open Gaps in the windows or doors Wet drywall or flooring in the basement If you see any of these warning signs, give us a call. We can come give a free estimate and provide you with permanent, cost-effective solutions. And should you need it, many of our products is backed by a full written warranty. We're confident that you'll be impressed with our systems, and we assure you that you'll get an effective repair at a reasonable price. Why Should I Fix My Foundation? We want you to have a safe, comfortable space to create a lifetime of amazing memories. Keep the following facts in mind: The Problem Will Get Worse : A foundation problem never gets better on its own. As it gets worse, the problem will cost more to fix. Resale Value : Who wants to buy a house with a foundation problem? Nobody! Appearance : Foundation problems often cause ugly cracks -- not only in the foundation itself but also inside the home. Door and Window Operation : As your foundation fails to hold the structure in place, your house will bend and twist. This will cause doors and windows to stick and jam. Use of Space : Sometimes you can lose the use of your space because of foundation failure. That's not what you paid for when you bought your home! A Safer Home : It's unusual, but disasters like foundations collapsing, chunks of brick veneer falling off the house, and other serious safety hazards do emerge. Keep Pests Away : Insects and animals can get into your home through cracks in the foundation, becoming unwanted and uninvited guests. Davenport Foundation Repair is built upon honesty, integrity and responsibility. For 35 years we have dedicated ourselves to providing permanent, cost-effective solutions to customers from Logan, UT to St. George, Utah. Part of our job is to educate our customers and help them determine where there is a problem. Concrete issues are very common. As the winter turns to spring homeowners may begin to notice changes in their concrete. So when should you call us? 1- If you slabs have raised or sunken. 2- If there are separations between your slabs of cement. 3- If your stairs have fallen and/or separated from the home’s foundation. These situations create safety hazards. Our PolyLevel foam can lift the concrete to level quickly and make your cement slabs safe and beautiful again. We appreciate the trust our customers give us to repair their homes and concrete slabs. We know you home is your most valuable asset. We want you have a safe place to have fun, relax and create memories. This video is one example of how we create a safe space for your home and family. You can find more information about our products under “Services” on our website. about_us_our_blog_28550_new_tools_for_be.text: Concrete Lifting Sidewalks in Utah | News and Events for Davenport Foundation Repair Schedule Annual Maintenance 1-801-569-2302 Proudly Serving Salt Lake City, West Valley City, Provo & Nearby 1-801-569-2302 Menu Services Foundation Repair Foundation Problems Foundation Repair Costs Foundation Repair Products Concrete Repair Cracked Concrete Concrete Sealant Sidewalk Repair Concrete Driveway Repair Concrete Expansion Joints Concrete Leveling Concrete Lifting Examples Interior Slab Leveling Lift & Level FAQ Photo Gallery Basement Waterproofing Our Waterproofing System Products Commercial Foundations Crawl Space Repair Crawl Space Waterproofing Structural Repairs Sump Pumps Photo Gallery Our Sump Pump Systems Installation Steps Repair & Maintenance Schedule Annual Maintenance Our Work Videos Before & After Testimonials Reviews Case Studies Photos About Us Technical Papers Job Opportunities Awards Meet the Team Our Blog Donations Affiliations Financing Service Area Payment Free Quote Our Blog Home » About Us » Our Blog » New Tools for Better Results New Tools for Better Results April 20th, 2017 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: New Tool Offers Customer Better Concrete Lifting Experience Having uneven concrete sidewalks, driveways or patios is an eyesore and a safety hazard. Our team is well trained and experienced in lifting concrete back to level. The process is quite amazing and coming soon, we have an improvement to offer our customers. The PolyLevel injection ports, used to insert a polymer foam into the concrete to lift it, will be only 3/8 of an inch in diameter. That’s approximately the same diameter as a ballpoint pen. This means the hole we drill to inject your concrete with PolyLevel will be ¼ of an inch SMALLER than before. Many companies use a 5/8 inch port, approximately the size of a dime. With such a small area to fill after the repair has been made, your concrete will be even more attractive. PolyLevel is polymer that consists of two separate liquids that are combined right at the injection nozzle to trigger a chemical reaction that turns the blended ingredients into expanding, high-density foam. The foam flows into voids and between loose soil particles, expanding to about 15 times its initial volume. This expansive action effectively lifts settled concrete. An experienced technician, like those at Davenport Foundation Repair, can control the application to create just the right amount of raising pressure. The polymer begins to harden quickly after doing its raising work. Within just 30 minutes, it reaches 90% of its final strength, enabling damaged concrete roads and slabs to be put back into service right away. The speed of polymer injection repairs is another huge advantage over mortar pumping. In addition to lifting and realigning settled and/or shifted concrete, polymer injection can be done prior to construction to improve soil stability and strength. Injections as deep as 20ft.-30ft. are possible. True, it may need a little TLC—some new paint, maybe new flooring and window treatments, but really it’s got great bones. You are so excited to sta rt your new adventure, but don’t forget to take a step back and really have the home evaluated to help avoid unwanted pitfalls and expensive repairs. It is a good idea to get a home inspected by a licensed professional before purchasing a home. Remember you want the bones of the home to be in great shape. Bones include things such as heating and cooling systems, the roof, electrical, plumbing and the foundation. When you have a home inspection done make sure they check the integrity of the basement, crawlspace or slab your potential new home is sitting on. Knowing you have a healthy foundation can provide peace of mind. If the home inspector finds something questionable, have the homeowner of your potential new place give us a call for a free estimate on a foundation repair, crawlspace repair or waterproofing. We will provide a written estimate so you are aware of the costs associated with any structural issues. The cost of the home is only one financial factor to consider when purchasing a home. Renovations, repairs and regular maintenance also need to be built into the buyer’s budget. Real Estate Broker Beth Campbell suggests buyers get an idea of how much renovation buyers can tolerate and to take an honest look at what home repair talents they really have. “I try to impart to my buyers the task before them, with eyes wide open!” says Campbell. Doing your homework can really pay off, and ensure your perfect home is just that! The White House, or “The People’s House,” is worth an estimated $399,042,879, according to a recent Zillow.com article. The White House has been called home by every American president except George Washington, who chose the site. It sits on 18 acres and is 55,000 square feet. The home includes the Executive Residence bordered by colonnades that connect to the West Wing and East Wing. Built in 1800 this historical landmark houses 16 bedrooms and 35 bathrooms. It does share some traits with many other, smaller scale homes. For instance it is cooled by central air, has a barbeque area, sprinkler system, fireplaces, double pane/storm windows and vaulted ceilings. It also has a few luxuries that many of us would love in our dream house. Those include a large basketball court, a movie theatre, large porticos, controlled security access, a tennis court, and an elevator. “The six-story Executive Residence serves as the president's living quarters and entertaining area. Notable rooms include the Diplomatic Reception Room where President Franklin D. Roosevelt held fireside chats, Lincoln Bedroom that was once the namesake's office, East Room which hosts large ceremonies and State Dining Room for formal dinners. The impressive kitchen is equipped to serve dinner for up to 140 guests and hors d'oeuvres to over 1,000,” according to Zillow. As we know from recent reports regarding President Trump’s move into The White House, the first family can change the top two floors of the residents to accommodate their personal needs. In addition to many bedrooms, you'll find a sun room, music room, game room and gym. Also within the house is a library, a doctor's office, flower and carpenter shops, and a bowling alley. Consider Repairing Your Sidewalk. Need a Big Bang for Your Buck? Consider Repairing Your Sidewalk. March 14th, 2017 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: Fixing your sidewalks is one of the best home improvement projects you can make. It’s been listed as one of the top 10 improvements you can do to your home. We know it’s not an improvement that is as alluring as some of the others on your list, but it does go a long way toward improving the safety and look of your home. Pouring new concrete may not be necessary. In the past, contractors often raised settled concrete by pumping a liquid mortar beneath the settled section (called mud jacking). But this pumping process is hard to control, and the added mass of the mortar puts even more weight on the soil. Fortunately, foundation and concrete repair specialists now have a new technique that's more effective at raising settled concrete. Polymer injection harnesses the expansive force of a structural grade geopolymer to provide fast concrete leveling , fill voids in soil and strengthen soil that has poor load-bearing qualities. The polymer consists of two separate liquids that are combined right at the injection nozzle to trigger a chemical reaction that turns the blended ingredients into expanding, high-density foam. The foam flows into voids and between loose soil particles, expanding to about 15 times its initial volume. This expansive action effectively lifts settled concrete. An experienced technician, like those at Davenport Foundation Repair, can control the application to create just the right amount of raising pressure. The polymer begins to harden quickly after doing its raising work. Within just 30 minutes, it reaches 90% of its final strength, enabling damaged concrete roads and slabs to be put back into service right away. The speed of polymer injection repairs is another huge advantage over mortar pumping. In addition to lifting and realigning settled and/or shifted concrete, polymer injection can be done prior to construction to improve soil stability and strength. Injections as deep as 20ft.-30ft. are possible. When buying a home location is everything. Many of us want an area with good schools, low crime and modern day conveniences nearby. While where our home is built is very important, what our home is built upon is just as significant. What determines the type of homes built in a certain area? The first consideration is the climate. If you live in the southwest desert, you need a home that will stay cool. In areas that experience yearly flooding, such as Southeast Asia, homes are built on stilts so the water runs beneath them. The next consideration is the types of materials available. In desert regions where trees are scare, homes are made of mud and grasses. People living in the mountains often build homes made from rocks and timber. In Utah we have a variety of geological and climatic conditions that need to be taken into consideration. Besides building a home with proper cooling and heating elements for our often- wild weather, the soil your house is built upon should be considered. According to Janis L. Boettinger of Utah State University, soils of the mountains and benches are slightly acidic to neutral with thick, dark-colored surface horizons, while soils of the deserts are alkaline and lightly colored. Extensive areas of outcropping rock, drifting sand dunes, and playa lakebeds also characterize the state of Utah. This means we have a variety of soil conditions that may affect your foundation. There are areas of the state where sandy soil is present and when dry, may allow for a home’s foundation to sink. We also have areas of blue clay that can cause a variety of foundation issues as well. When foundations sink and cause damage to the home such as cracks in the interior walls, doors and windows that are difficult to open or stair step cracking in the exterior brick, you need to call an expert to fix it. Breaking Records! February 23rd, 2017 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: We Are Breaking Records! The history of construction is fascinating. From the pyramids in ancient Egypt to the Burj Khalifa in Dubai, humankind has been building and breaking records since the beginning. Davenport Foundation Repair has also had a record breaking year. The Great Pyramid of Giza Was the Tallest Building in the World for Over 3,800 Years The Great Pyramid of Giza is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World, and for good reason. From its completion around 2560 BC to 1311 AD it was the tallest building in the world. Since it was replaced by Lincoln Cathedral in England as the tallest building in the world, no other building has held the title for longer than 250 years. The Hoover Dam Could Take You From California to the New York Island The Hoover Dam was a truly massive undertaking during its construction from 1931 to 1936. To put it in perspective, the 3,250,000 cubic yards of concrete used in the construction of the Hoover Dam would be enough to build a two-lane highway over the nearly 3,000 mile stretch of land between San Francisco and New York City. The Chrysler Building’s Spire Was a Secret During Construction Back in the 1920s tall buildings were popping up all over New York City, so much so that constructing tall buildings became a competition of sorts. The architect for the Chrysler Building , William Van Alen, was locked in a heated competition with fellow architect H. Craig Severance (who was building the 40 Wall Street building) to see who could build the taller building. Van Alen wanted to ensure his building ended up taller than Severance’s so he made secret plans to add a 185-foot spire to the very top of the building at the conclusion of its construction. The addition of the spire gave the Chrysler Building bragging rights as the tallest building in the world—for 11 months (it was eclipsed by The Empire State Building in 1931). Facts about Concrete and our PolyLevel Foam Concrete is one of the oldest, most durable building materials. Egyptians used it as an infill material for the pyramids. Romans mixed lime, water and volcanic ash from Mount Vesuvius to create “pozzolana” ancient concrete building material. The Romans built the Pantheon using concrete. The dome on the Pantheon is still the world's largest unreinforced concrete dome. Thomas Edison held 49 concrete patents and experimented with precast concrete houses filled with concrete furniture, pianos and refrigerators. Concrete is used twice as much in construction than all other building materials like reinforcement, timber, etc. It is the most used material in the world in terms of volume. Reinforced concrete has high resistance to fire and water. Concrete is only of the only materials used for underwater structures such as dams and submerged bridge piers. So what happens when this amazing material sinks and cracks? Davenport Foundation Repair uses a revolutionary product called PolyLevel to raise the concrete to level. Strong but light. PolyLevel® weighs only about 4lbs. per cubic ft., compared to 120lbs. per cubic ft. for standard fill material. PolyLevel® ’s light weight makes it useful where denser fill material might impose an undesirable load on weak soils. Despite its light weight, PolyLevel® can support substantial loads; it typically provides greater lifting power than mudjacking. Waterproof. Once cured, PolyLevel® will not wash away. PolyLevel® ’s waterproofing properties can be beneficial in certain applications. Stable and inert. PolyLevel® does not react with soil or moisture; it will not leach harmful chemicals into the soil. Quick curing. Down time is minimized with PolyLevel® concrete repair. Full loading of the foundation, roadway or other structural element can usually happen about 15 minutes after the material is injected. Adjustable. Adjusting the density and expansive force of the 2-part foam affords a wide range of geotechnical uses. Lifting force can be adjusted by fine-tuning the chemical reaction that causes the foam to expand. An experienced applicator can factor not only the weight of the structural element but also soil characteristics and temperature and weather conditions. Special formulations are possible for applications where water must be displaced. Noninvasive. PolyLevel® injection equipment isn’t bulky, enabling applicators to access confined areas. When properly injected, PolyLevel® is not as messy or disruptive as other slab and foundation-lifting techniques. Is your foundation stable and dry? January 31st, 2014 by Davenport Foundation Repair Categories: Investing in a stable and dry foundation in Utah is a home-saving project. Do you have vertical cracking, sticky doors or windows, stair step cracking or uneven floors; possibly you may have leaking basement cracks or floor seepage, a wet crawlspace or water entering though window well cracks? A poor concrete foundation can drastically decrease the value of your property and cause future damage to the structure of your home. A high quality preventative repair project will protect your high dollar investment. We specialize in foundation stabilization, basement waterproofing and leveling of concrete slabs, sidewalks, driveways, etc. Call us today 1-801-569-2302 for a free estimate and find out about our new Poly-Level system. Not only is it cost effective, it comes with a three-year warranty and is a green alternative to concrete replacement. Due to their design and ease to install, they are most commonly used whenever soil conditions prevent standard foundation solutions. Instead of requiring large excavation work, they thread into the ground. This minimizes installation time, requires little soil disturbance, and most importantly transfers the weight of the structure to load bearing soil.
