View More Before & After Photos Related Videos Push Pier Installation in Provo See All YouTube Videos Job Stories From Provo, UT Concrete Walkway & Driveway Repair in Provo, UT Location: Provo, Utah Services Provided: PolyLevel® Concrete Lifting, NexusPro® Joint Sealant, SealantPro™ Concrete Protection System Products Used: 77.10 lbs of PolyLevel® 245 ft of NexusPro® 965 sq ft of SealantPro™ Duration: 1 Day Customer Satisfaction: ✅ Very happy with the results The Problem A homeowner in Provo, UT, noticed a growing void beneath their front walkway near the home’s entry. The sidewalk section adjacent to the foundation had visibly settled, creating a potential tripping hazard and an unsightly gap. The hollow space beneath the slab raised concerns about further concrete cracking, water pooling near the foundation, and damage spreading to the connected driveway slab. Utah’s seasonal moisture changes and soil settlement patterns often lead to these types of voids, especially in walkways that aren’t properly compacted during construction. The Solution Our crew performed a full evaluation and recommended a 3-part Concrete Protection System designed to stabilize, protect, and extend the life of the affected concrete areas: PolyLevel® Injection : We used 77.10 lbs of PolyLevel® to fill the void beneath the concrete walkway. This high-density polyurethane foam expands immediately upon injection, lifting and leveling the slab with precision. Unlike mudjacking, PolyLevel doesn’t add weight to the soil, making it ideal for long-term stabilization. NexusPro® Joint & Crack Sealant : Once the slab was leveled, we sealed 245 linear feet of joints and cracks using NexusPro®. This flexible, UV-resistant sealant keeps out moisture and debris—preventing further erosion and joint widening. SealantPro™ Protective Coating : Finally, we applied SealantPro™ across 965 sq ft of concrete surface. This hydrophobic coating bonds with the concrete at a molecular level, offering permanent protection from water, road salts, and stains. It helps reduce long-term wear, especially in Utah’s freeze-thaw cycles. The Result In just one day, the walkway and driveway were fully restored—with no demolition, no replacement, and no extended downtime. The void was eliminated, the slab leveled, and the surface sealed and protected. The homeowner was thrilled with the outcome, noting the visual improvement and peace of mind knowing their entryway was now safe and secure. He reached out to Davenport Foundation Repair with a clear goal: stop the damage from spreading and protect the concrete for the long haul. The Problem: Spalling, Settlement, and a Sinking RV Pad The homeowner reported signs of spalling —a common issue in Utah where freeze-thaw cycles and moisture infiltration cause the surface of the concrete to flake or peel away. Additionally, he was concerned about settling under the RV pad in the backyard, which had created uneven surfaces and small trip hazards. Like many properties in Saratoga Springs , this home is built on soil that can shift over time, especially during dry summers or after heavy rainfall. The combination of soil movement and exposure to the elements had led to uneven concrete slabs and failing caulking between joints. Left unaddressed, the damage could worsen, leading to more costly repairs down the line. Our Solution: PolyLEVEL® Injection & NexusPro® Joint Sealant Davenport Foundation Repair scheduled a 3-day job to restore the driveway and RV pad. The repair process was carefully planned in phases to ensure each step provided long-term value: Step 1: PolyLEVEL® Injection We began by lifting and leveling the sunken concrete slabs using our high-precision PolyLEVEL® system . This two-part expanding polyurethane foam is injected beneath the concrete, gently raising the slabs back to their original position. Unlike traditional mudjacking, PolyLEVEL® is lightweight, cures quickly, and won’t wash out or add stress to the soil. This step was critical for the RV pad, which had sunk due to poor soil compaction. PolyLEVEL® filled the voids beneath the concrete and reestablished a strong, stable base—perfect for handling heavy loads like an RV. Step 2: Caulk Removal Next, we removed the old, deteriorating caulk from the driveway joints and cracks. A clean surface is essential for a proper seal, so our team took extra care during this step to avoid leaving behind debris or residue. Step 3: NexusPro® Crack and Joint Repair Finally, we applied NexusPro® , a flexible, UV-resistant joint sealant developed to handle extreme temperature swings common in Utah’s climate. NexusPro® bonds tightly to concrete and remains flexible over time, which helps prevent water from entering the joints and causing further erosion or spalling. The sealant was carefully smoothed for a clean, professional finish that not only looked great but offered long-term waterproofing protection. The Outcome: Safe, Sealed, and Stable Concrete The transformation was dramatic. What began as a spalling, uneven driveway is now a clean, level, and sealed surface that’s ready to handle daily use—and RV parking—with confidence. The homeowner was especially pleased that the repair was minimally disruptive and completed in just three days. With PolyLEVEL® lifting the slabs and NexusPro® sealing the cracks, this Saratoga Springs home is now protected from further concrete damage, soil movement, and seasonal moisture changes. Signs of Foundation Settlement at the Grantsville Home One of the most noticeable symptoms was a vertical crack running through several courses of exterior brick near a window. In some areas, the movement had created visible gaps between sections of the masonry. These types of cracks can develop as portions of a foundation settle at different rates. As the foundation moves, the materials above it can be subjected to stress, resulting in cracks and separation in brick, mortar, drywall, and other parts of the home. Rather than simply addressing the visible cracks, the Davenport Foundation Repair team evaluated the structure to determine where foundation stabilization was needed. Identifying the Area That Needed Stabilization The project plan documented elevation differences throughout the affected portion of the home and identified the section of the foundation requiring stabilization. Based on the findings, a system of seven push piers was planned along the affected foundation walls. The piers were strategically positioned to support the portion of the structure experiencing settlement. This approach addresses the underlying foundation problem instead of treating cracking as an isolated cosmetic issue. Installing 7 Push Piers to Stabilize the Foundation To install the push pier system, the Davenport Foundation Repair crew excavated at each designated pier location to expose the home's foundation footing. Heavy-duty brackets were then secured at the foundation. Steel push pier sections were hydraulically advanced into the ground until they reached competent load-bearing material capable of supporting the structure. Once the required resistance was achieved, the seven-pier system could be used to transfer the affected portion of the home's structural load away from the weaker soils immediately beneath the foundation and onto more reliable bearing material below. After stabilization was completed, the excavated areas could be backfilled and the property restored. The Problem: Sinking & Cracking in a High-Traffic Area Concrete driveways are exposed to some of the harshest conditions, especially in Utah, where freeze-thaw cycles, dry spells, and clay-rich soil can wreak havoc on slabs. In this case, the right side of the driveway, adjacent to a covered parking area, had visibly dropped. The settling created misalignment along the joints, making it difficult to walk, drive, or park comfortably. Complicating matters was a significant amount of caulking and sealant that had deteriorated over time. Cracks and joints no longer had proper protection, which meant moisture intrusion was likely contributing to voids forming under the slab . If left unaddressed, the damage could quickly escalate, leading to larger cracks, broken edges, or full slab failure. Precision Lifting with PolyLevel® We used 175 pounds of PolyLevel , a high-density polyurethane foam, to lift and level the settled slab. This product is injected through small, dime-sized holes drilled into the concrete surface. Once injected, it expands rapidly, filling voids and lifting the slab back into its proper position — often within minutes. This approach is perfect for Utah’s varied soils because it doesn’t wash out, shrink, or degrade over time like mudjacking. Unlike store-bought caulks, NexusPro remains flexible and UV-resistant, so it won’t dry out, crack, or peel under the hot West Jordan sun. 3. The lifted slab was level with adjacent sections, eliminating trip hazards and improving water drainage. The new NexusPro sealant created clean, uniform joints that will resist weathering for years to come.
